The growing prevalence of Accepted 16 September 2025 kratom products enriched with 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-HMG), an active metabolite of mitragynine Available online 22 September 2025 (MG), necessitates evaluating the respiratory effects of these alkaloids and determining whether naloxone reverses their potential respiratory depressant effects. Respiratory parameters were measured Key words: in awake, freely moving female and male Sprague-Dawley rats using whole body plethysmography. To Kratom minimize handling-induced artifacts and ensure precise respiratory recordings, drugs were adminis­ Mitragynine 7-Hydroxymitragyine tered intravenously. Morphine and 7-HMG induced signiﬁca cant respiratory depression, evidenced by Respiratory depression reductions in breathing frequency, tidal volume, and minute volume. The potency of 7-HMG to decrease Opioid overdose minute volume by 50% was 4.5-fold greater than that of morphine. In contrast, MG administration unexpectedly increased respiratory frequency. Naloxone fully reversed the respiratory depression induced by both morphine and 7-HMG but did not alter the respiratory stimulant effects produced by MG. These ﬁndings demonstrate that 7-HMG exhibits signiﬁca cant respiratory depressant properties similar to classical opioids, and importantly, such depressant effects are effectively antagonized by naloxone. Conversely, MG exerts respiratory stimulant effects through mechanisms independent of opioid receptor pathways. Collectively, these data highlight crucial pharmacological distinctions be­ tween kratom alkaloids, underscoring the risk associated with high 7-HMG—containing kratom prod­ ucts and suggesting that the predominant alkaloid MG may offer a safer respiratory proﬁle le. Significance Statement: The prevalence of kratom products containing 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-HMG), a μ-opioid receptor agonist, underscores the need to evaluate respiratory effects of kratom-related al­ kaloids and their reversal by naloxone. 7-HMG induced signiﬁca cant respiratory depression comparable with morphine, which was reversed by naloxone. Conversely, mitragynine, kratom’s most abundant alkaloid, unexpectedly increased respiratory frequency unaffected by naloxone. These ﬁndings highlight critical pharmacological differences between kratom-related alkaloids, emphasizing potential risks associated with products containing high concentrations of 7-HMG. © 2025 American Society for Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics.
